did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with an urgent cry to the Lord: “I call to you, hurry to me,” followed immediately by a request to listen to the voice of the one praying.
Did you know? David compares his prayer to incense and the lifting of his hands to the evening offering, presenting prayer as an act of sacrifice before the Lord.
Did you know? In this verse, David asks for his speech to be guarded in two ways: “Guard my mouth” and “keep watch over the door of my lips.”
Did you know? David asks not only that his mouth be guarded, but also that his heart not turn toward evil and that he not take part in the deeds and delicacies of the wicked.
Did you know? David describes a righteous person’s correction as kindness, and even when it pains him, he prefers it to adopting the ways of the wicked.
Did you know? The verse uses vivid, compressed imagery to describe the downfall of the wicked, and concludes by saying that they listen to David’s words because they are pleasant.
Did you know? David describes his distress and that of his people through the image of earth being split open and plowed, while their bones are scattered near the grave.
Did you know? Despite the danger he describes, David does not give up hope: his eyes are turned toward the Lord, and he declares that the Lord is his refuge.
Did you know? David asks for protection from two kinds of dangers mentioned in the chapter: “traps” and “snares”—images of the traps prepared for him by evildoers.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a contrast between the wicked, who fall into their own traps, and David, who asks to continue on safely.
